Subject: Post-demo: Deployment & compliance requirements

Anna — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we can align on the hosting path that meets your security needs:

- Summary of the ask: you need a deployment that supports PHI under HIPAA, signed BAA, and evidence of SOC2 Type II controls for data handling. You also mentioned a desire to keep logs for 7 years and to have audit support for an upcoming vendor pass in Q3.

- Deployment options we covered (short):
  * Hosted API (Redwood-managed): fastest, we can sign a BAA and provide our SOC2 report + supplemental controls. Regional data residency available in us-west and us-east clouds.
  * Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool): isolated tenant with network restrictions, improved throughput SLA, still hosted by Redwood but with stronger logical isolation and contract terms.
  * Private (VPC / on-prem): customer-controlled VPC or an on-prem bundle — highest isolation and auditability; longer lead time and additional ops work.

Next steps / asks from you:
1) Confirm which deployment mode you want us to prioritize (Hosted / Dedicated / Private). If you need to evaluate all three, let us know the top blockers that matter most (BAA alone? SOC2 evidence? On-prem requirement?).
2) Please share the internal audit checklist or the specific items the compliance team will request (if available).

I'm attaching the BAA draft and a short SOC2 summary so your legal and security teams can review before we put formal paperwork in flight.

Proposed timeline if MedClarity prioritizes Hosted or Dedicated: we can produce an evidence bundle and a draft BAA within 5 business days; Dedicated provisioning (reserved capacity) can be scheduled in 2–3 weeks once contract terms are agreed. Private/on-prem will need a preliminary scoping call — estimate 4–6 weeks.

Happy to schedule a short follow-up with security/ops next week. If you want, I can also pull Monica (Customer Success) and Karthik (solutions) into that call.

Thanks,
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Anna Ruiz <anna.ruiz@medclarity.ai>

Thanks, Tessa — good recap. A few clarifications from our security team:

- BAA: yes, MedClarity requires a signed BAA before any PHI is processed.
- SOC2: we require the vendor's SOC2 Type II report (last 12 months) and a short mapping of how Redwood's controls map to our audit requirements (control owners / control frequency).
- Audit support: our external auditors will want a point of contact and copies of select evidence (change management, access logs, data deletion policies). We understand some items are redacted; that’s fine as long as we can validate controls.
- Data residency: primary processing needs to be in the US. Secondary DR can be elsewhere but must be documented.
- On-prem: it's a hard preference for a subset of our PHI workflows, but not a strict blocker — if Redwood can provide Dedicated + strict network isolation + audit traceability, that may be acceptable.

I'll attach our internal vendor-security checklist for reference (separate email from security@medclarity.ai). For timelines, we need a compliance packet in ~10 business days to make the Q3 audit window.

Can you confirm who at Redwood will own the evidence collection and whether Dedicated will provide the logs/access auditors need?

—Anna
Anna Ruiz
Head of Product Ops | MedClarity
